BrainGnomes can collect existing QC evidence into a study inventory, export it
as TSV tables and an R object, and render a Quarto dashboard. The dashboard
provides searchable React tables, interactive plots, and expandable details
linking outputs to their diagnostics and recorded workflow attempts.

## Collect a snapshot

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(BrainGnomes)
scfg <- load_project("/path/to/project")
qc <- collect_qc_inventory(scfg)
qc

# Optional: include participants whose data have not arrived yet.
qc <- collect_qc_inventory(
  scfg,
  subjects = data.frame(sub_id = c("001", "002"), ses_id = "baseline")
)

# Optional: use a saved request's settings and realized scope (not proof it ran).
run_qc <- collect_qc_inventory(scfg, run_id = "latest")

subset(qc$inventory, output_status == "missing")
subset(qc$workflow, status %in% c("FAILED", "BLOCKED", "NOT_TRACKED"))
subset(qc$coverage, attention)
```

Collection reads the configuration, tracking database, file metadata, and small
diagnostic files. It does not read image arrays, rerun processing, submit work,
or update the database. By default, job states come from the tracking database.
Use `refresh = TRUE` to also request the existing read-only scheduler comparison
for active jobs. The report identifies whether that comparison was performed.
Collection reports its phases and derivative counts; use `quiet = TRUE` to
suppress these messages. Only the original FD column is read from wide confounds
tables, with each source summarized once per collection. Manifest size/mtime
observations are reused across repeated historical associations.

The returned `bg_qc_inventory` object includes these tables:

| Table | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `acquisitions` | Discovered raw BOLD files, preserving participant, session, task, run, acquisition, direction, echo, and other filename entities |
| `inventory` | Discovered/expected derivative records by stage and stream, including source/atlas paths, availability, saved audit status, and convenient numeric QC columns |
| `workflow` | Configured participant/session/stage expectations and current tracked work units, including project setup jobs |
| `coverage` | Raw-acquisition/stage/stream observations and unresolved units, including raw BOLD without resolved derivatives |
| `metrics` | Numeric values with units, definitions, source files, and available/missing observation counts |
| `regions` | Per-label usable voxel proportions, retention status, and recorded exclusion reasons |
| `evidence` | Source/report/diagnostic paths, availability, size, and modification time |
| `checks` | Saved postprocessing checks, full messages, warnings, timestamps, elapsed seconds, and structured details as JSON |
| `jobs`, `attempts` | Historical job records and logical attempts, preserving current-attempt indicators |
| `manifest_files` | Exact paths in historical output manifests and current size/mtime comparisons |
| `active`, `reconciliation` | Active-job timing and optional scheduler comparisons |
| `issues` | Collection errors and ambiguous or unsupported evidence |

`record_id` joins derivative-related tables **within a snapshot**. Snapshot IDs,
collection times, schema version, and package version are in `qc$metadata`.
They also travel with the TSV bundle in `snapshot.json`.
Use `readRDS("inventory.rds")` to recover all R column types. When importing TSVs,
read BIDS identifier columns as character strings to preserve leading zeros.

## Render the dashboard

Rendering requires [Quarto 1.4 or newer](https://quarto.org/docs/dashboards/) and
the optional R packages below. Inventory collection and TSV/RDS export remain
available without these rendering dependencies.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("reactable", "plotly", "htmltools", "htmlwidgets", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))

html <- render_qc_dashboard(qc, "/path/to/reports/qc-snapshot-01")
browseURL(html)

# Export only the machine-readable snapshot to a separate directory.
write_qc_inventory(qc, "/path/to/exports/qc-snapshot-01")
```

Each export requires a new or empty directory. Render a new snapshot when the
study changes; an existing report remains a record of what was observed at its
collection time. If Quarto fails, the RDS and TSV exports remain available and
`render.log` retains the failure details even in quiet mode. `render-status.json`
records the result. Rendering uses a temporary writable Quarto cache, including
on systems with a read-only home directory. Retry from the retained export
without rescanning the project:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
html <- render_qc_dashboard("/path/to/reports/qc-snapshot-01")
```

A successful HTML report cannot be overwritten. Rendering also accepts an
exported directory and a different new output directory.

### Cohort → review list → participant

1. Start with the scope banner and **Acquisition coverage**, then resolved-path
   availability, required audits, and grouped
   attention reasons. Failures, missing/invalid evidence, and descriptive concerns are
   separate review categories. Multiple derivative products supporting the same
   acquisition/context/reason are grouped; expand to inspect their evidence.
   Coverage/workflow review items can have no derivative to expand: these are
   unresolved expectations, not zero-of-zero successes. Submission uncertainty
   is a separate review item. Collection issues remain separately available.
2. On **QC metrics**, choose a compatible comparison group. The default
   **histogram** shows a cohort distribution without hundreds of participant
   labels. **ECDF** shows the cumulative fraction of recorded source values.
   Counts report observed sources, participants, and unavailable recorded values.
   A missing diagnostic file is not a recorded metric value: consult the
   attention list for missing evidence. Neither view applies exclusion cutoffs.
3. Sort the **review sources** table by value to locate extremes. Participant
   identity, value, and unit appear first. Select a participant to switch to its
   **participant scans** plot and open original MRIQC/fMRIPrep reports and saved
   computational checks. Click a scan point or choose a derivative output for
   exact source and manifest associations. **Return to cohort** clears the
   participant selection while preserving other shared filters and returns the
   chart to view. Participant details sit directly beneath the changing chart.

The same participant/session/task/stage/stream/space controls are available on
every page and stay synchronized. A pinned scope bar shows the current selection,
collection time, and scheduler-query status; **Edit scope** returns to the current
page's selectors, and **Reset** clears shared filters. Scoped counts, distributions, and tables use
the fields actually recorded at their own grain. For example, raw acquisitions
respond to participant/session/task but do not have processing stream or stage;
workflow units can cover multiple scans and do not respond to task/space.
FD is an upstream acquisition measurement: downstream stage/stream selections
retain FD through the selected outputs' input chain or raw coverage identities,
rather than discarding it because it was produced by fMRIPrep. Space selections
still require a matching spatial output association.
Each table lists its scope fields. Settings and participant-wide report links
are context, not acquisition-level measurements. Whole-snapshot collection
issues, manifest comparisons, and active/scheduler context are explicitly
labeled and do not change with the shared scope. Scheduler **not queried** is
distinct from having no active database records or no comparison rows.

Table searches and column filters refine only that table, not the charts or
headline counts. **Export matching rows (all pages)** downloads all currently
matching table rows, including off-page rows, directly from the embedded data.
The TSV/RDS links in **Downloads & interpretation** always download the complete,
unfiltered snapshot. Neither type of export changes the collected inventory.

The four dashboard pages cover the overview, derivative exploration, QC metrics,
and workflow/evidence details. Manifest views show grouped association counts,
distinct paths, and a labeled preview of at most 200 exceptions; the preview's
table export contains only displayed preview rows. The full `manifest_files.tsv`
and RDS retain every association. Tables use
[reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/), with client-side filtering,
sorting, pagination, and expandable rows. Plotly charts provide hover values
and source distributions. Compatible groups retain units, processing stage,
stream, session, task, space, resolution, and atlas identity. Unknown atlases
in separate diagnostic directories are not pooled. Mean FD has the same
definition across tasks and is pooled; each original confounds source is counted
once **after** scope filtering, so selecting a different output space does not
lose its observations. Individual scans are not averaged together. Missing
values remain visible in the review table.

The HTML embeds its JavaScript and styles and does not require a running R
session, web server, or network connection for those interactions. Evidence,
checks, and manifest associations are indexed once; expanded detail panels are
built only when requested, rather than pre-rendering thousands of nested tables.
Keep the
HTML with its neighboring TSV/RDS files for downloads. Evidence links point to
original project files using paths relative to the report directory: moving
only the report does not copy upstream HTML, its assets, logs, or imaging data.
On a remote cluster, download the report bundle and open the HTML locally; a
desktop browser may not be able to open a remote `file://` URL. Native report
links still require the source filesystem, and those upstream reports may use
external interactive dependencies even though the dashboard itself is offline.
Browser or hosting policies may restrict links to local files. The table retains
the full source paths so users can still locate the evidence.

## Interpret counts and metrics

Workflow units, acquisitions, and derivative records have different
denominators. A participant-level fMRIPrep job can cover several sessions and
acquisitions. A BOLD acquisition can generate several spatial representations,
postprocessing streams, atlas time series, and connectivity matrices. The
dashboard labels these counts separately. **Resolved output paths available**
does not measure cohort completion: participants with raw BOLD but no resolved
fMRIPrep paths remain visible in coverage and Needs attention. Coverage counts
raw files once per selected stage/stream, not once per spatial representation.
Missing echo entities can represent combined-echo outputs; coverage does not
guess the intended number of spatial/echo products. AROMA has workflow context
but no inferred file-coverage guarantee.

Expected native derivative paths are resolved from discovered upstream images
and the **current stream configuration**, following the production filename
conventions. Before an upstream image exists, the configured work remains in
the workflow table; output spaces and multi-echo combinations are not guessed.
The subject scope includes discovered files and BIDS participant directories,
tracked subjects, saved run subject tables, and any explicitly supplied subjects.
Historical scope remains visible even if the current configuration has changed.

With `run_id`, expectations instead use the saved configuration and realized
participant/session scope, selected stages and streams, and exact retry units.
Subject-wide retry stages such as AROMA follow the same exact-unit selection as
submission; they are not crossed with every selected participant. The scope
banner and browser title identify the run. Recorded submission state and counts
of acknowledged/tracked jobs distinguish a saved retry request from a confirmed
execution. Missing acknowledgements require inspection of provenance and job
recovery; do not blindly resubmit, since an allocation may have been accepted
without an acknowledgement. Available files may predate that request.
The snapshot records the run ID, provenance path, selected stages, and settings.
This mode requires resolved run provenance and cannot be combined with
`subjects`, which adds project-wide expectations. Files and manifest comparisons
still describe the current filesystem, rather than historical reconstruction.
Existing native outputs are retained when their upstream images are no longer
available; unavailable stream/source attribution is left missing.

A file marked `available` exists and is nonempty. A completed job describes its
recorded workflow outcome. A saved audit marked `passed` describes its recorded
computational check. These observations do not establish scientific image
quality. Audit timestamps remain available because an audit can outlive the
derivative it describes. Output manifests provide exact historical path
associations, using size and modification time checks rather than content hashes.
A subsequent failed attempt does not acquire ownership of an older output.
Filename-shaped historical stream labels remain in the tracking download and
the workflow's `reported_stream`/`stream_attribution` columns. They are excluded
from the shared Stream selector rather than guessed into a configured stream.

The `attention` field highlights missing/empty derivatives, invalid or failed
audits, malformed diagnostics, saved ROI loss, shared destination paths, and
failed/blocked/cancelled workflow context, missing required checks, and saved
audit warnings. `attention_reasons` explains the flags in plain language. `workflow_status`, `workflow_scope`,
and `workflow_run_id` identify the current participant/session-level context;
they do not identify the producing attempt for the derivative.
It is a navigation aid and does not define analysis inclusion or exclusion.

- `mean_fd` summarizes finite `framewise_displacement` values in the original
  fMRIPrep confounds TSV, in millimeters. The metric table records the finite and
  missing frame counts. Postprocessed FD may have been filtered, demeaned, or
  censored; it is not substituted for this source metric.
- MRIQC IQMs retain separate names: `mriqc_fd_mean`, `mriqc_tsnr`,
  `mriqc_dvars_std`, and `mriqc_gcor`. These are imported summaries with their
  [upstream definitions](https://mriqc.readthedocs.io/en/stable/iqms/bold.html).
  Their observation denominators are unavailable when not recorded by MRIQC.
- Censor metrics count ones in the saved binary mask, where one means retain.
  A saved mask does not establish that physical volume removal was executed.
  Processing settings separately show scrubbing enabled, application to volumes,
  interpolation, and its rule; configured settings do not prove execution.
- ROI metrics summarize the recorded extraction retention rule and usable voxel
  proportions. The regional table preserves label-level losses and their
  recorded reasons, including `outside_mask`, `invalid_bold`, and
  `below_threshold`. Losses are specific to the atlas and input stream.

Optional diagnostics are not generated by collection. Enable native
`validate_postproc_steps` or ROI `save_diagnostics` in the processing
configuration when those records are wanted for future processing. Absent evidence is `not_applicable` when its check is disabled or does not
apply to that stage, `missing` when required, and `unavailable` when the
requirement is unknown. Existing evidence is retained even if its setting is
now disabled. The header explicitly identifies disabled validation instead of showing a
misleading zero-of-zero pass. Empty check/ROI sections distinguish stages not
selected from absent saved evidence. Expanding checks shows full messages,
warnings, timings, and scalar measurements; arrays remain in `checks.tsv` JSON.
Selected mask replay, smoothness, intensity, and spectral measurements are also
available as numeric metrics with units and saved sampling counts. No human ratings, review lifecycle,
inclusion decisions, or automatic motion thresholds are implemented.

The exports contain participant identifiers and source paths. Share them with
the same access controls as the study's existing reports.

## Maintainer browser regression

Regular unit tests exercise grouping, source deduplication, empty/legacy
snapshots, inert JSON encoding, and the shipped JavaScript without a browser.
The opt-in walkthrough renders 500 synthetic participants with two scans each
and opens the HTML directly from disk, checking desktop/mobile scope, histogram
and ECDF views, participant navigation, lazy evidence, original HTML links,
all-page and empty filtered exports, and scheduler empty states. It uses locally
installed tooling and never downloads a browser or contacts the scheduler:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
export BRAINGNOMES_TEST_QC_BROWSER=true
export BRAINGNOMES_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE=/path/to/node_modules/playwright-core
export BRAINGNOMES_CHROMIUM=/path/to/chromium
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "qc-inventory")'
```

Quarto and Node must be on `PATH`; optional rendering packages must be installed.
Run this only where local Chromium launches are permitted. The fixtures contain
placeholder images, not real imaging data or evidence of scientific quality.
